newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Prostitutes bring HIV to Romanian village.
newsitem.headline: Prostitutes bring HIV to Romanian village.

text.p: More than half the residents of a Romanian village have been infected with the virus causing AIDS after many of its women went off to a Black Sea port to work as prostitutes, a newspaper reported on Saturday.

The daily Cronica Romana quoted officials at the main hospital in the port of Constanta as saying that more than half the population in the nearby village of Garliciu carried the HIV-virus. It did not give exact figures of those affected.
"The disease spread through unprotected sexual intercourse of these women with fellow villagers," Rodica Matusa, a well-known expert in Romania on Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, told the daily.
"Prostitutes from Garliciu have operated in the port and abroad and come back 'enriched' to their native village."
Officially statistics show that Romania has 2,300 AIDS sufferers, but only 200 are adults. A total of 272 adults are listed as HIV-carriers.
More than 3,500 children have been infected with HIV through injections and blood transfusions -- accounting for more than half of Europe's paediatric AIDS cases.
Romania also has one of the lowest rates in eastern Europe for use of condoms as a contraceptive, though family planning has made some progress since the fall of Communism in 1989.
Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu banned abortions to help boost the national birth rate and most means of contraception were unavailable until after his overthrow and execution in 1989.
